scope: Mechanism diagnostic with frozen cap samples, ridge regularization, normalization and coefficients. Replay all 122 RGB-texture and RGB-only score fields and metadata exactly before evaluating frozen RGB classifiers on a new grid. Synthetic comparisons use the same 320-pixel evaluation frame and known labels, replacing the 320-to-160-to-320 scoring path with direct RGB at 320; known synthetic corners are privileged. Real classification uses exact stored production crop RGB at its original target resolution, with the same source coverage. Retain all 32 inspected development photos and six unresolved crops, including wrong crop proposals. No retraining or crop changes; no per-photo method selection. Freshly fit all 26 native masks with ten seconds of search and the unchanged production fitter, then independently render and audit editable SVGs. Previous production, RGB-only and neutral-deviation fits remain frozen comparison references; no speed claim from unmatched wall-clock runs. Neither synthetic training views nor inspected real photos are an untouched holdout.
questions: Does removing the reduced scoring grid improve known synthetic boundary accuracy when the fitted classifier stays fixed?
Which thin details and straight corners change on the complete real cohort?
Do native-resolution masks survive fitting and editable export, or expose remaining classifier/search failures?
gates: Exact prior field and fit-metadata replay; abort on disagreement, do not weaken it.
Identical crops, observed regions and resolutions; no omitted unresolved photos.
Keep existing geometry, material, feature and mask-error checks; empty-cut candidates must also pass the independent editor audit.
Record every result and inspect all real photos plus the preselected 21 synthetic examples.
productionChanges: None. These results guide material-model design; the classifier is not automatically adopted.
